name: Bahrain
note: Arabic is the sole authoritative language. English translations are produced for commercial laws but are not authoritative. Hijri dates appear alongside Gregorian in official publications; FRBR URIs use Gregorian year only, with Hijri stored as FRBRalias.

hierarchy.note: Codes only (Civil Code, Commercial Code). Most laws do not use Book.
Primary higher division. Arabic 'Bab'. English translations inconsistently render as 'Part', 'Chapter', or 'Book' — always map to AKN part. Ordinal numbering: 'Part One' / الباب الأول.
Secondary higher division within a Part. Arabic 'Fasl'. English may render as 'Chapter' or 'Section' — always map to AKN chapter.
Basic citable unit. Continuous Arabic numeral numbering throughout, never restarting per Part or Chapter. Format in text: 'Article (5)' with parentheses.
First subdivision of an article. Arabic numerals in parentheses: (1), (2), (3). English translations sometimes call these 'paragraphs'.
Second subdivision. Lowercase letters in parentheses in English: (a), (b), (c). Arabic original may use Arabic-script letters or continuing numerals.
Third subdivision. Present in complex codes. Exact numbering format (Roman, Arabic, sub-letters) not confirmed from direct document inspection.

legislative_decree.label: Legislative Decree
legislative_decree.note: Issued by the King between parliamentary sessions or during dissolution. Structurally identical to primary Laws. FRBRsubtype: 'legislative-decree'. Share the same article number sequence per year as Laws.

constitution.label: Constitution

hierarchy.note: Primary division. E.g., 'Chapter I. The State', 'Chapter IV. Public Authorities'.
Secondary division within some Chapters. E.g., 'Section 1. The King', 'Section 2. The Executive Authority'.

constitution.note: Constitution of the Kingdom of Bahrain, issued February 14 2002, with amendments through 2017.

royal_decree.label: Royal Decree
royal_decree.note: Non-legislative royal acts: appointments, treaty ratifications, establishment of bodies. Typically short (2-5 articles). FRBRsubtype: 'royal-decree'. Use only when digitising such decrees explicitly.

frbr.note: Laws and Legislative Decrees share the same URI pattern and number sequence per year. Instrument type is recorded as FRBRsubtype in metadata. Hijri year stored as FRBRalias.

numbering.insertion_note: Civil law bis/مكرر convention expected. Inserted Article 10 → 'Article 10 bis' / 'المادة 10 مكرر'.

enacting_formulae.text: We, [King's name], King of the Kingdom of Bahrain, having reviewed the Constitution and [list of laws reviewed], and pursuant to what was approved by the Shura Council and Council of Representatives, have promulgated the following law:
enacting_formulae.note: Exact Arabic text not read verbatim from official PDF — verify before production use.

enacting_formulae.text: We, [King's name], King of the Kingdom of Bahrain, having reviewed the Constitution and [list of laws reviewed], and given urgent necessity requiring action that cannot be delayed, and pursuant to the submission of the Minister of [...], have issued the following Legislative Decree:
enacting_formulae.note: The preamble typically lists all laws and decrees reviewed, often spanning a full page.

amendments.phrasing: Article (N) of [Law citation] shall be amended to read as follows: / shall be cancelled / The following Article shall be added after Article (N):
amendments.note: Wholesale replacement (new law repealing predecessor) is also common for major legislation. Amendment laws cite predecessor by type, number, year, and subject title.

structuring.prompt_additions: Bahrain uses ARTICLE as the basic unit (مادة, maddah), not SECTION. The hierarchy is: BOOK (codes only) > PART (Bab, باب) > CHAPTER (Fasl, فصل) > ARTICLE > SUBSECTION (numbered clauses, بند) > PARAGRAPH (lettered items, فقرة). Article numbering is continuous throughout the law regardless of Part/Chapter boundaries. Article numbers appear in parentheses in text: 'Article (5)'. English translations may inconsistently render Bab as 'Chapter' and Fasl as 'Section' — normalise to PART/CHAPTER in all cases. The Constitution uses CHAPTER > SECTION (as higher div) > ARTICLE.

supranational_memberships.note: GCC Unified Laws require transposition into domestic legislation via Law or Legislative Decree — no direct effect. Bahraini implementation appears as a distinct domestic instrument. GCC instruments may be referenced at /akn/gcc/act/{year}/{number} (proposed — no established AKN precedent).
UN Security Council Chapter VII resolutions are binding on Bahrain as a member state but require domestic implementation legislation.

display.bilingual_note: lloc.gov.bh and bahrainbusinesslaws.com publish English translations alongside Arabic originals. Arabic (ara) expression is primary/authoritative; English (eng) expression is a translation.

validation.note: Public reference profile; synthetic XML controls do not certify corpus coverage.
